question: What is the correct order of organisation in the human body?
What is the role of bile in digestion?
options: It digests proteins into amino acids
It emulsifies fats and neutralises stomach acid
It breaks down starch into sugars
It absorbs water from undigested food
correct: It emulsifies fats and neutralises stomach acid

question: Which enzyme breaks down starch?
What happens to an enzyme when it is denatured?
options: Its active site changes shape permanently
correct: Its active site changes shape permanently

question: Where is bile produced?
Which blood vessel carries oxygenated blood away from the heart to the body?
Which chambers of the heart pump blood out to the lungs and body?
What is the function of valves in the heart?
options: To pump blood around the body
To prevent the backflow of blood
To carry oxygen to heart muscle
correct: To prevent the backflow of blood

question: Which blood vessel has the thickest walls?
What is a malignant tumour?
options: A tumour that stays in one place and does not spread
A tumour that spreads to other parts of the body
A tumour caused only by smoking
A tumour that is always fatal
correct: A tumour that spreads to other parts of the body

question: Which component of blood carries oxygen around the body?
Which tissue transports water and mineral ions up the plant?
What controls the opening and closing of stomata?
What causes coronary heart disease?
options: A viral infection of the heart muscle
A build-up of fatty plaques in the coronary arteries
A lack of red blood cells
Damage to the heart valves by bacteria
correct: A build-up of fatty plaques in the coronary arteries

question: What do villi do in the small intestine?
options: Increase the surface area for absorption
correct: Increase the surface area for absorption

question: An enzyme's shape is changed permanently by high temperatures. This is called being __________.
The enzyme __________ breaks down proteins into amino acids.
Bile is produced by the __________ and stored in the gall bladder.
The __________ are the upper chambers of the heart that receive blood.
Blood vessels called __________ carry blood away from the heart.
The liquid part of blood that carries dissolved substances is called __________.
The loss of water vapour from plant leaves through the stomata is called __________.
__________ tissue transports dissolved sugars from leaves to the rest of the plant.
A tumour that spreads to other parts of the body is described as __________.
The wave-like muscular contractions that move food along the digestive system are called __________.
Match each enzyme to the food molecule it breaks down.

pairs.definition: Breaks down proteins into amino acids
Breaks down lipids into fatty acids and glycerol

question: Match each blood vessel to its correct description.

pairs.definition: Carries blood away from the heart, thick muscular walls, no valves
Carries blood towards the heart, thin walls, has valves
One cell thick, site of exchange between blood and tissues

question: Match each digestive organ to its function.

pairs.definition: Produces protease and hydrochloric acid to digest proteins
Produces amylase, protease and lipase enzymes
Main site of digestion and absorption of nutrients
Absorbs water from undigested food to form faeces

question: Match each plant tissue to its function.

pairs.definition: Transports water and mineral ions from roots to leaves
Transports dissolved sugars from leaves to the rest of the plant
Control the opening and closing of stomata
Packed with chloroplasts — main site of photosynthesis in the leaf

question: Match each blood component to its function.

pairs.definition: Carry oxygen around the body using haemoglobin
Help blood to clot at a wound
Liquid that carries dissolved nutrients, hormones and waste

question: State what is meant by the term enzyme.
mark_scheme: A biological catalyst (1) that speeds up chemical reactions without being used up (1) — accept either point.

question: Name the blood vessel that supplies the heart muscle with oxygenated blood.
mark_scheme: Coronary artery (1).

question: State the difference between a benign and a malignant tumour.
mark_scheme: Benign tumour stays in one place / does not spread (1); malignant tumour spreads to other parts of the body (1) — accept either point for 1 mark.

question: State the function of stomata in a leaf.
mark_scheme: Allow gas exchange (1) / allow water vapour to escape during transpiration (1) — accept either.

question: Explain why enzymes are described as specific.
mark_scheme: Each enzyme has a specific active site (1); only one substrate fits the active site — lock and key model (1); so each enzyme only catalyses one type of reaction (1) — any two.

question: Explain why the small intestine is well adapted for absorption.
mark_scheme: Villi increase the surface area (1); villi have a good blood supply to maintain a concentration gradient (1); villi have thin walls for a short diffusion distance (1) — any two.

question: Describe the function of arteries and veins.
mark_scheme: Arteries carry blood away from the heart (1); veins carry blood towards the heart (1); arteries have thick muscular walls (1); veins have valves to prevent backflow (1) — any two.

question: Explain how guard cells control the opening of stomata.
mark_scheme: When guard cells gain water they become turgid and change shape (1); this opens the stomata (1); when they lose water they become flaccid and stomata close (1) — any two.

question: Explain how a stent is used to treat coronary heart disease.
mark_scheme: A stent is a metal mesh tube (1); inserted into a narrowed coronary artery (1); it holds the artery open / restores blood flow to the heart muscle (1) — any two.

question: Explain the role of bile in the digestion of fats.
mark_scheme: Bile is produced in the liver (1); stored in the gall bladder (1); emulsifies fats — breaks large fat droplets into smaller ones (1); increases surface area for lipase to work (1); bile is alkaline and neutralises stomach acid (1) — any three.

question: Describe the structure and function of capillaries.
mark_scheme: Capillaries are the smallest blood vessels (1); walls are one cell thick (1); short diffusion distance for exchange of substances (1); large network provides large surface area (1); substances such as oxygen and glucose diffuse into tissues (1) — any three.

question: Explain how increasing temperature affects enzyme activity, including what happens above the optimum temperature.
mark_scheme: Increasing temperature increases rate of reaction (1); more enzyme-substrate collisions (1); above optimum temperature the enzyme denatures (1); active site changes shape (1); substrate no longer fits (1) — any three.

question: Explain what transpiration is and describe the factors that affect its rate.
mark_scheme: Transpiration is the loss of water vapour from leaves through stomata (1); light intensity — more light increases rate (1); temperature — higher temperature increases rate (1); humidity — lower humidity increases rate (1); wind speed — more wind increases rate (1) — any three.

question: Explain how the digestive system breaks down a meal containing starch, protein and fat, naming the enzymes involved and where they act.
mark_scheme: Amylase breaks down starch in the mouth and small intestine (1); protease breaks down proteins in the stomach and small intestine (1); lipase breaks down fats in the small intestine (1); bile emulsifies fats increasing surface area for lipase (1); products absorbed in the small intestine (1) — any four.

question: Describe the double circulation of blood in the human body, including the role of the heart.
mark_scheme: Blood travels from the heart to the lungs to pick up oxygen (1); returns to the heart (1); then pumped to the rest of the body (1); heart has four chambers — two atria and two ventricles (1); left side pumps oxygenated blood to body (1); right side pumps deoxygenated blood to lungs (1) — any four.

question: Evaluate the use of statins and stents as treatments for coronary heart disease.
mark_scheme: Statins lower cholesterol levels (1); reduce risk of fatty plaques forming (1); must be taken long-term / side effects possible (1); stents hold arteries open physically (1); immediate effect (1); risk of surgery / blood clots (1); statins are a preventive treatment, stents are a cure (1) — any four.

question: Explain what cancer is and describe the difference between benign and malignant tumours. Include risk factors for cancer in your answer.
mark_scheme: Cancer is uncontrolled cell division (1); benign tumour stays in one place (1); malignant tumour spreads to other tissues / metastasis (1); risk factors include smoking / UV radiation / viral infections / inherited genes (1); lifestyle factors can increase or decrease risk (1) — any four.

question: Explain how the structure of the small intestine is adapted to maximise the absorption of digested food molecules.
mark_scheme: Villi increase the surface area for absorption (1); microvilli on villi further increase surface area (1); villi have a rich blood supply — maintains concentration gradient (1); walls are one cell thick — short diffusion distance (1); large intestine absorbs water (1); lacteals in villi absorb fatty acids and glycerol (1) — any five.

question: A patient is diagnosed with coronary heart disease. Explain what causes this condition, the symptoms it produces, and the treatments available.
mark_scheme: Fatty plaques build up in the coronary arteries (1); arteries become narrowed (1); blood flow to heart muscle is restricted (1); heart muscle receives less oxygen (1); symptoms include chest pain / angina / heart attack (1); treatments: statins lower cholesterol (1); stents hold arteries open (1); bypass surgery uses another blood vessel to go around the blockage (1) — any six.

question: Evaluate the lifestyle changes and medical treatments available to reduce the risk of cardiovascular disease. In your answer, refer to both advantages and disadvantages.
mark_scheme: Lifestyle: healthy diet reduces cholesterol (1); exercise strengthens heart muscle (1); stopping smoking reduces risk (1); no side effects from lifestyle changes (1); requires willpower and long-term commitment (1). Medical: statins reduce cholesterol effectively (1); may have side effects (1); stents give immediate relief (1); surgery carries risk (1); medical treatments may be needed when lifestyle changes are insufficient (1) — any six.

question: Explain the levels of organisation in a multicellular organism, from cell to organism. Give an example at each level.
mark_scheme: Cell: smallest unit of life, e.g. muscle cell (1); tissue: group of similar cells working together, e.g. muscle tissue (1); organ: group of tissues working together, e.g. stomach (1); organ system: group of organs working together, e.g. digestive system (1).

question: Describe the role of enzymes in digestion. Include where amylase, protease and lipase act and what they break down.
mark_scheme: Amylase breaks down starch into sugars (1) — produced in salivary glands and pancreas (1); protease breaks down proteins into amino acids (1); lipase breaks down lipids into fatty acids and glycerol (1).

question: Explain why the heart has two separate sides and describe the route blood takes through the heart.
mark_scheme: Right side pumps deoxygenated blood to the lungs (1); left side pumps oxygenated blood to the body (1); blood enters right atrium from vena cava, goes to right ventricle, to lungs via pulmonary artery (1); returns oxygenated via pulmonary vein to left atrium, left ventricle, then aorta to body (1).

question: Describe the structure and function of red blood cells, white blood cells and platelets.
mark_scheme: Red blood cells: biconcave, no nucleus, contain haemoglobin — carry oxygen (1); white blood cells: have nucleus, can change shape — defend against infection by engulfing pathogens or producing antibodies (1); platelets: cell fragments, no nucleus — involved in blood clotting (1); all three found in plasma which transports dissolved substances (1).

question: Explain how coronary heart disease develops and why it can lead to a heart attack.
mark_scheme: Fatty deposits (atheroma) build up inside coronary arteries (1); this narrows the lumen of the artery — restricts blood flow (1); a blood clot may form at the site of the deposit (1); this can completely block the artery, cutting off oxygen supply to heart muscle, causing a heart attack (1).

question: Evaluate lifestyle changes versus medical treatments (statins and stents) for reducing the risk of coronary heart disease.
mark_scheme: Lifestyle: diet low in saturated fat reduces cholesterol (1); regular exercise strengthens heart muscle (1); stopping smoking reduces risk of clot formation (1). Medical: statins lower cholesterol but have side effects (1); stents keep arteries open but require surgery (1) — award 4 marks for balanced evaluation.

question: Explain the difference between benign and malignant tumours. Include what happens to cells in each type.
mark_scheme: Benign tumours: cells divide uncontrollably but remain in one place (1); do not spread to other tissues (1); malignant tumours: cells invade neighbouring tissues (1); cells can break off and spread via blood/lymph to other parts of the body (metastasis) (1).

question: Describe how the pH of the digestive system varies and explain how this affects enzyme activity.
mark_scheme: Stomach is acidic (pH ~2) — produced by hydrochloric acid (1); small intestine is alkaline (pH ~8) — bile neutralises acid (1); each enzyme has an optimum pH — e.g. pepsin works best at pH 2 (1); above or below optimum pH, enzyme shape changes / active site denatures — rate of reaction falls (1).

question: Explain the differences in structure between arteries, veins and capillaries, linking each to its function.
mark_scheme: Arteries: thick muscular walls, narrow lumen — withstand high pressure from heart (1); veins: thinner walls, wider lumen, valves — blood at lower pressure, valves prevent backflow (1); capillaries: one-cell-thick walls — allow diffusion of substances to/from tissues (1); capillaries form networks near cells to reduce diffusion distance (1).

question: Describe the role of the liver in the human body. Include at least three different functions.
mark_scheme: Produces bile to emulsify fats (1); regulates blood glucose — converts excess glucose to glycogen (1); breaks down excess amino acids — deamination producing urea (1); detoxifies alcohol and other harmful substances (1). Accept: produces heat / stores vitamins / produces blood clotting proteins.

question: Explain how the immune system responds when a pathogen enters the body for the first time. Include the roles of antibodies and memory cells.
mark_scheme: White blood cells detect antigens on the pathogen (1); lymphocytes produce specific antibodies that bind to those antigens (1); antibodies neutralise or destroy the pathogen (1); memory cells remain in the blood after infection — produce antibodies rapidly if same pathogen enters again (1).

question: Explain how the small intestine is structurally adapted to maximise the absorption of digested food products.
mark_scheme: Villi increase surface area (1); microvilli on epithelial cells further increase surface area (1); rich blood supply — maintains concentration gradient for diffusion (1); thin walls — short diffusion distance (1); long length of small intestine — more time for absorption (1).

question: Describe the cardiac cycle. Include what happens in the atria, ventricles, and what role valves play in ensuring one-way blood flow.
mark_scheme: Atria contract, pushing blood into ventricles (1); ventricles contract, pushing blood out to lungs (right) and body (left) (1); valves between atria and ventricles (atrioventricular) close to prevent backflow (1); semilunar valves at base of arteries prevent backflow when ventricles relax (1); cycle repeats at resting rate of ~70 beats per minute (1).

question: Evaluate the use of artificial hearts as a treatment for heart failure. Include advantages, disadvantages and an ethical consideration.
mark_scheme: Advantage: can keep patient alive while waiting for donor heart (1); no risk of rejection as no biological tissue (1); disadvantage: mechanical parts can fail (1); anticoagulant drugs needed to prevent blood clotting (1); ethical: very expensive, so access may be unequal (1).

question: Explain how lifestyle factors can increase the risk of cancer. Include at least three different risk factors and the type of cancer associated with each.
mark_scheme: Smoking: lung cancer — carcinogens in smoke cause mutations in DNA (1); UV radiation from sun: skin cancer — UV damages DNA in skin cells (1); obesity/high fat diet: bowel or breast cancer — excess oestrogen in fat tissue (1); alcohol: liver cancer — liver processes alcohol, leading to DNA damage (1); these factors increase the chance of a mutation in a tumour-suppressor gene (1).

question: Describe how blood transports oxygen from the lungs to respiring cells. Include the role of haemoglobin and the conditions that affect oxygen release.
mark_scheme: In lungs: oxygen binds to haemoglobin to form oxyhaemoglobin (1); red blood cells travel in blood plasma to respiring tissues (1); in tissues: high CO₂ / lower pH causes haemoglobin to release oxygen (1); oxygen diffuses into cells down concentration gradient (1); CO₂ is picked up and transported back to lungs dissolved in plasma / as bicarbonate ions (1).

question: Explain how enzymes work using the lock-and-key model. Include the effect of temperature on enzyme activity and explain what happens when an enzyme is denatured.
mark_scheme: Enzyme has an active site with a specific shape (1); substrate fits into active site — complementary shape (lock-and-key) (1); increasing temperature increases rate — more kinetic energy, more collisions (1); above optimum temperature: bonds in enzyme break, active site changes shape (1); enzyme is denatured — substrate can no longer fit, reaction stops (1).

question: Evaluate the use of monoclonal antibodies in medicine. Include how they are produced, one medical use, and one limitation.
mark_scheme: Produced by injecting a mouse with antigen — mouse produces B lymphocytes (1); B lymphocytes fused with tumour cells to form hybridoma cells (1); hybridoma cells divide and produce large quantities of identical (monoclonal) antibodies (1); use: cancer treatment — antibodies carry radioactive/toxic drugs directly to tumour cells (1); limitation: can cause side effects; expensive to produce; can trigger immune reactions in patients (1).

question: Explain what happens when food reaches the stomach. Include the role of hydrochloric acid, the enzyme present, and the physical processes involved.
mark_scheme: Stomach produces hydrochloric acid — creates pH 2 (1); acid kills most bacteria in food (1); acid provides optimum pH for pepsin (1); pepsin is a protease — breaks proteins into shorter polypeptide chains (1); muscular stomach wall churns food — physical digestion, increases surface area (1).

question: Describe the double circulatory system of mammals. Explain the advantage of this system compared to a single circulatory system.
mark_scheme: Pulmonary circulation: heart → lungs → heart (1); systemic circulation: heart → body → heart (1); blood returns to heart after visiting lungs so pressure is restored (1); oxygenated and deoxygenated blood are kept separate (1); allows higher blood pressure to be maintained to the body — more efficient delivery of oxygen (1).

question: Explain why high blood pressure is a risk factor for cardiovascular disease. Include the effects on arteries and the heart.
mark_scheme: High blood pressure puts excessive force on artery walls (1); damages the inner lining of arteries — makes them more prone to fatty deposit formation (1); increases risk of atherosclerosis — narrowing of arteries (1); heart must work harder to pump blood — can lead to heart failure over time (1); risk of blood vessel rupture / stroke increases (1).

question: Evaluate the use of blood transfusions and artificial blood substitutes in emergency medicine. Consider the advantages and disadvantages of each.
mark_scheme: Blood transfusions: provide all components including platelets and clotting factors (1); but require blood type matching to prevent rejection (1); artificial substitutes: no need for matching (1); do not carry disease risk (1); but cannot carry oxygen as effectively as red blood cells / limited shelf life (1).

question: Explain how the digestive system processes a meal containing starch, protein and fat from ingestion to absorption. Name the enzymes and organs involved.
mark_scheme: Mouth: amylase in saliva begins breaking starch into maltose (1); stomach: HCl and pepsin begin protein digestion — proteins → polypeptides (1); small intestine: pancreatic amylase, protease (trypsin) and lipase continue digestion (1); bile from liver/gall bladder emulsifies fats — increases surface area for lipase (1); final products absorbed: glucose, amino acids, fatty acids, glycerol across villi into bloodstream (1); large intestine absorbs water, waste passes out as faeces (1).

question: Evaluate lifestyle and medical interventions for coronary heart disease. Consider their effectiveness, risks, and accessibility.
mark_scheme: Lifestyle — diet: reducing saturated fat lowers LDL cholesterol, reducing plaque build-up (1); exercise strengthens heart, lowers resting heart rate, reduces blood pressure (1); Statins: lower cholesterol, shown to reduce heart attack risk; side effects include muscle pain (1); Stents: physically open narrowed arteries; procedure risk; may re-narrow (1); Heart transplant: most effective for end-stage disease but donor shortage and need for immunosuppressants (1); lifestyle changes most cost-effective and without medical risk, but compliance is difficult (1).

question: Describe the role of the immune system in responding to infection by bacteria. Include the innate response, the adaptive response, and how vaccination can provide protection.
mark_scheme: Innate: phagocytes engulf and destroy bacteria (phagocytosis) (1); adaptive: lymphocytes recognise specific antigens on bacteria (1); B-cells produce specific antibodies that bind to bacterial antigens (1); antibodies neutralise toxins / agglutinate bacteria for destruction (1); memory cells remain after infection — secondary response is faster and stronger (1); vaccination: introduces weakened/dead antigens — immune system produces memory cells without causing disease (1).

question: Explain the biological basis of cancer. Include the role of mutations, tumour-suppressor genes, and how cancer treatments such as radiotherapy and chemotherapy work.
mark_scheme: Cancer caused by mutations in genes that control cell division (1); mutations in tumour-suppressor genes allow cells to divide uncontrollably (1); proto-oncogene mutations can switch on cell division permanently (1); radiotherapy: ionising radiation kills rapidly dividing cancer cells (1); but also damages nearby healthy tissue — causes side effects (1); chemotherapy: drugs target dividing cells throughout body (1); useful for widespread cancer but also affects healthy rapidly dividing cells (hair follicles, gut lining) (1) — any 6 points.

question: Explain how enzyme activity is affected by temperature, pH and substrate concentration. For each factor, describe the shape of the graph and explain the biology.
mark_scheme: Temperature: rate increases up to optimum (more kinetic energy, more collisions) (1); above optimum rate falls — enzyme denatured, active site shape changes (1); pH: rate highest at optimum pH; above or below, ionic bonds in enzyme break, active site shape changes (1); both sides show decrease — different enzymes have different optima (1); substrate concentration: rate increases with concentration as more substrate molecules available (1); rate plateaus when all active sites are occupied (enzyme is saturated) (1).

question: Evaluate the use of monoclonal antibodies in the diagnosis and treatment of disease. Include pregnancy tests, cancer treatment, and any ethical or practical limitations.
mark_scheme: Pregnancy tests: monoclonal antibodies detect hCG hormone in urine — highly specific and rapid (1); cancer diagnosis: antibodies labelled with radioactive markers locate tumour cells (1); cancer treatment: antibodies carry toxic drugs directly to tumour — reduces damage to healthy tissue (1); advantages: highly specific, can be produced in large quantities (1); limitations: expensive to produce, side effects in some patients (1); ethical: hybridoma production uses animal experimentation (1).

question: Describe the structure of the heart and explain how its structure is adapted for its function as a double pump. Include the roles of the chambers, valves, and coronary arteries.
mark_scheme: Four chambers: two atria (receive blood) and two ventricles (pump blood out) (1); right side: receives deoxygenated blood, pumps to lungs; left side: receives oxygenated blood, pumps to body (1); left ventricle wall is thicker than right — must pump blood further at higher pressure (1); valves (bicuspid, tricuspid, semilunar) ensure one-way blood flow (1); coronary arteries supply heart muscle itself with oxygen and glucose (1); if coronary arteries blocked → heart attack as muscle cannot respire (1).

question: A patient has been diagnosed with a malignant tumour. Evaluate the treatment options available, considering how each targets cancer cells and the potential side effects.
mark_scheme: Surgery: physically removes tumour — effective for localised cancer (1); risk of infection, does not treat metastasised cells (1); radiotherapy: targeted radiation kills cancer cells by damaging DNA (1); damages nearby healthy tissue, causes fatigue and skin burns (1); chemotherapy: drugs target all rapidly dividing cells throughout body (1); kills cancer cells but also damages hair follicles, digestive lining — hair loss, nausea (1). Accept immunotherapy / monoclonal antibodies for full mark.

question: State the correct order of organisation from cell to organ system.
mark_scheme: Cell → tissue → organ → organ system (1); all four levels in correct order (1).

question: Give two products of the digestion of proteins.
mark_scheme: Amino acids (1); the substrate is broken down by protease enzymes (1) — award both marks for: amino acids and that protease catalyses this. Accept: two named amino acids for both marks.

question: Describe the role of platelets in the blood.
mark_scheme: Platelets are small cell fragments (1); they help blood to clot at a wound site to prevent blood loss and entry of pathogens (1).

question: Explain why the left ventricle wall is thicker than the right ventricle wall.
mark_scheme: The left ventricle pumps blood to the whole body (1); it needs to generate more force / higher pressure than the right ventricle which only pumps to the lungs (1).

question: Give two features of the small intestine that increase the rate of absorption.
mark_scheme: Villi / large surface area (1); good blood supply / thin walls / short diffusion distance (1) — any two distinct features.

question: State two risk factors for coronary heart disease.
mark_scheme: High cholesterol diet (1); smoking (1); high blood pressure (1); lack of exercise (1); obesity (1) — any two.

question: Describe the difference between xylem and phloem tissue.
mark_scheme: Xylem transports water and mineral ions (1); phloem transports dissolved sugars / products of photosynthesis (1).

question: Explain what is meant by a benign tumour.
mark_scheme: A benign tumour is a mass of cells that divide uncontrollably (1); but it remains in one place and does not spread to other parts of the body (1).

question: Compare the structure of arteries and veins.
mark_scheme: Arteries have thicker, more muscular walls than veins (1); veins have valves to prevent backflow, arteries do not (1).

question: Name the enzyme that digests fats and state where it is produced.
mark_scheme: Lipase (1); produced in the pancreas / small intestine (1).

question: Explain what is meant by the terms tissue, organ and organ system, giving one example of each.
mark_scheme: Tissue: group of similar cells working together, e.g. muscle tissue (1); organ: group of tissues working together for a function, e.g. stomach (1); organ system: group of organs working together, e.g. digestive system (1).

question: Describe the role of the stomach in digestion.
mark_scheme: Stomach produces hydrochloric acid which creates an acidic pH (1); stomach produces protease enzymes (pepsin) to begin protein digestion (1); muscular stomach wall churns food, increasing surface area for enzyme action (1).

question: Explain how valves in the heart ensure one-directional blood flow.
mark_scheme: Valves open when pressure is higher on one side (1); they close when pressure drops to prevent blood flowing backwards (1); this ensures blood flows in the correct direction through the heart and into the major arteries (1).

question: Describe the structure of a red blood cell and explain how it is adapted to carry oxygen.
mark_scheme: Biconcave disc shape gives a large surface area for gas exchange (1); no nucleus so more room for haemoglobin (1); packed with haemoglobin which combines with oxygen to form oxyhaemoglobin (1).

question: Explain three lifestyle factors that can increase the risk of cancer.
mark_scheme: Smoking — carcinogens damage DNA in lung cells (1); exposure to UV radiation — damages DNA in skin cells (1); excessive alcohol consumption — damages liver cells and increases risk of liver cancer (1); obesity / poor diet linked to bowel and breast cancer (1) — any three.

question: Describe three factors that increase the rate of transpiration in plants.
mark_scheme: Higher temperature increases rate — water evaporates faster (1); increased light intensity — stomata open wider (1); lower humidity — steeper water vapour concentration gradient (1); higher wind speed — blows away water vapour, maintaining gradient (1) — any three.

question: Explain the lock-and-key model of enzyme action.
mark_scheme: Each enzyme has an active site with a specific shape (1); only one substrate fits into the active site — like a key in a lock (1); when substrate binds, enzyme catalyses the reaction and products are released; the enzyme is unchanged (1).

question: Compare the functions of arteries, veins and capillaries.
mark_scheme: Arteries carry blood away from the heart at high pressure (1); veins carry blood back to the heart at low pressure with valves to prevent backflow (1); capillaries are the site of exchange of substances between blood and body tissues — one cell thick (1).

question: Explain how statins reduce the risk of coronary heart disease.
mark_scheme: Statins are drugs that lower the level of cholesterol in the blood (1); lower cholesterol reduces the formation of fatty plaques in coronary arteries (1); this reduces the risk of arteries becoming narrowed and reduces the chance of a heart attack (1).

question: Describe three functions of the liver in the human body.
mark_scheme: Produces bile to emulsify fats in digestion (1); breaks down excess amino acids by deamination, producing urea (1); regulates blood glucose by converting glucose to glycogen (1); detoxifies alcohol and harmful substances (1) — any three.

question: Explain how white blood cells defend the body against infection.
mark_scheme: Phagocytes engulf and digest pathogens by phagocytosis (1); lymphocytes produce specific antibodies that bind to antigens on pathogens (1); memory cells are formed so a faster response occurs if the same pathogen returns (1).
